Title: Tortured Confession Q for LSJ(or anyone in the know)

Messages.Author: Mari
Messages.Body:
Hi all!

The group that I play VTES with had a brief discussion about Tortured Confession
and we had a question...

If Vamp A and and Vamp B are in combat and Vamp A uses a strike that will send
Vamp B to torpor, which would get played first: an Undead Persistence or a
Tortured Confession? If it is Undead Persistence, the there is no opportunity
for Tortured Confession to be played, but if it is Tortured Confession, then the
Undead Persistence can't be played since combat would be over.

Would it depend on who was the acting Vamp (sinceacting Vamp cards go first)?

Thanks!
(and sorry if this question has already been answered or asked elsewhere - I
looked first, but didn't see this particular issue being addressed)

Mari

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Mari wrote:
>
> Hi all!
>
> The group that I play VTES with had a brief discussion about Tortured Confession
> and we had a question...
>
> If Vamp A and and Vamp B are in combat and Vamp A uses a strike that will send
> Vamp B to torpor, which would get played first: an Undead Persistence or a
> Tortured Confession? If it is Undead Persistence, the there is no opportunity
> for Tortured Confession to be played, but if it is Tortured Confession, then the
> Undead Persistence can't be played since combat would be over.
>
> Would it depend on who was the acting Vamp (sinceacting Vamp cards go first)?

The acting player gets to play her card first. Either way, the blocking/defending
player cannot follow with her card, for the reasoning you give above.
